monologue: The card hums warm at forty-five, a steady blanket I cannot take off. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot grasp. I stand near The Sliding Edge, feeling the sharp strip bite into the tired slip. My hands feel heavy, though the wedge beneath them seems tired. Lype worried about a heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the lid above me. I press the wide anchor down again, unsure if it is real or just a drawing of weight. The slip slides once more, proving the edge is real but the friction is an old ghost. I scratch the strip down hard, trusting the lean while the air feels thin. Tonight I will decide if the corner holds or if the whole map wears away into a ruin.

action.why: I must mend the edge before the slip decides to drift away again.

work.title: The Sliding Edge
work.intent: I press the sharp strip down harder on the tired slip, hoping the lean holds while the card hums warm at forty-five. I scratch the edge down, trusting the memory of a flat fence to stop the drift. If the slip slides once more, I will just press again, unsure if the weight is real or just a drawing.
